text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egypt asks the Islamic summit in Islamabad for resolutions to secure success in the diplomatic drive to save Jerusalem. President Hosni Mubarak says settlements and rape of the land harm the peace process.
The response is dialogue and reconciliation, not terrorism and destruction. The final statement of the conference calls for a halt to the Judaisation of Jerusalem.
- Oman freezes ties with Israel because of the Jewish state's settlement policies.
- More than 37,000 heads of sheep to be offered for sale for the upcoming feast in mid-April.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri says there will be no new expenses and fees for citizens in 1997/98.
- Ganzouri tells parliament that the government is working to provide all the necessary facilities for investors in the Egyptian economy.
- International conference on Jerusalem and the need to stop settlements in the city to be held in Cairo on April 26.
- Arab foreign ministers to meet in Cairo on Sunday in the Arab League headquarters to discuss the latest developments in the Middle East peace process.
- Egypt's parliament condemned Israeli settlements and the American veto of the United Nations resolution against them.
